key_insight: The paper turns hyperfine intermediate states from a source of error into a control resource to speed up adiabatic CNOT gates while maintaining high fidelity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to faster, more robust Rydberg-atom quantum gates that better fit within coherence-time constraints.
method: Use an EIT-based adiabatic CNOT protocol with two pathways: STAY and TRANSFER.
Exploit appropriately chosen hyperfine intermediate states to improve adiabaticity and accelerate population transfer.
Optimize pulse shapes and extend the model to include decay from multiple intermediate states and arbitrary state counts.
evidence_signal: In realistic cesium atomic setups, the optimized protocol achieves gate fidelities above 0.9991 in 0.3903 microseconds.
watch_item: Performance will still depend on controlling decay and decoherence from intermediate states, which may become more challenging as the state manifold grows.
paper_title: Fast Adiabatic Quantum Gates via Hyperfine Intermediate States
